name: C-PEPTIDE
description: C-Peptide measures the connecting peptide cleaved from proinsulin during insulin production. This test evaluates endogenous insulin secretion and helps differentiate between type 1 and type 2 diabetes mellitus.

testdeatils.instrumentation: Abbott Architect, Roche Elecsys, Beckman Coulter

literatureReview: C-Peptide is a byproduct of insulin synthesis, released in equimolar amounts with insulin. It has a longer half-life than insulin and better reflects beta-cell function. Normal fasting range is 0.8-3.5 ng/mL. Low levels suggest type 1 diabetes or advanced beta-cell failure. Normal/elevated levels indicate type 2 diabetes or insulin resistance. The test helps differentiate diabetes types, assess residual beta-cell function, and monitor disease progression. Chemiluminescent immunoassay provides high sensitivity. Unlike insulin, C-peptide is not affected by exogenous insulin therapy. Used in insulinoma diagnosis (elevated) and factitious hypoglycemia evaluation. Results interpreted with clinical context and concurrent glucose/insulin measurements.
